newsitem.title: JAPAN: Three Japanese firms halt sales of "24-hour" baths.
newsitem.headline: Three Japanese firms halt sales of "24-hour" baths.

text.p: Inax Corp and two other Japanese companies have suspended sales of "24-hour bath" units after the government asked them to check the products' safety, a Trade Ministry official said on Monday.

The Ministry of International Trade and Industry (MITI) official said that the other two makers were Sekisui Chemical Co Ltd and Hitachi Chemical Co Ltd. The official said the ministry did not know if other bath makers had stopped sales of the "24-hour bath" units, which automatically purify, circulate and heat water.
Inax and Sekisui said they had stopped selling the units for the time being but added that this would not affect their overall earnings as their volume of sales of such products was small.
Hitachi Chemical was not immediately available for comment.
Another 24-hour bath maker, Janome Sewing Machine Co Ltd, said it had not stopped sales.
The bath unit circulates water in the system so that warm water can be available in a bath tub all day long. Such systems are increasingly popular in Japan.

The ministry official said MITI informed companies in December that it was concerned that a pneumonia-causing bacterium, legionella pneumophila, could grow in the system. The ministry asked makers and sellers to check the safety of the product, he said.
"We could not prove the degree of safety by the ministry so we stopped shipments in December," an Inax spokesman said.
"We expect the ministry to come up with some decision after obtaining reports from companies, and we will consider our future action after seeing the ministry's conclusion," he said.
"We have stopped selling '24-hour bath' units but the decision is only temporary," a Sekisui spokesman said.
The ministry is now collecting data from companies and will submit it to a meeting of experts to be held on Wednesday before reaching a decision on the issue, the ministry official said.
Inax's shares fell 18 yen from Friday's close to 802 yen in Monday morning trade on the Tokyo Stock Exchange.
Sekisui shares were down 30 yen at 1,010 yen at midday but Hitachi shares were up 11 yen at 912 yen.
Janome's shares were ask-only at 260 yen at midday compared with Friday's close of 300 yen.
